title: Chery TIGGO 9 makes drivers miss a car they don’t even own yet in new campaign via Dentsu Creative
summary: The work arrives at a moment of significant momentum for Chery, whose popularity is surging, just three years after retu...
story: Built around the idea “Once you drive the TIGGO 9, you can’t undrive it,” the campaign dramatises the longing that follows an experience that unexpectedly resets your expectations.

The work arrives at a moment of significant momentum for Chery, whose popularity is surging, just three years after returning to the Australian market. With that growth comes an opportunity to keep changing perceptions of the brand.

Chery’s strong consideration-to-conversion performance suggested the bigger challenge wasn’t simply selling the TIGGO 9, but making more Australians want to experience it for themselves. Massage seats. Automatic park assist. Super Hybrid technology. Unexpected comfort and refinement.

Once you’ve had them, you miss them when they’re gone. A series of films turns that feeling into a campaign, with drivers unable to shake the memory of the TIGGO 9 after returning to their everyday lives.

The result is less conventional automotive product demonstration and more automotive separation anxiety. Says Zac Pritchard, Executive Creative Director, Dentsu Creative: “When you jump into the driver’s seat of a TIGGO 9, you realise just how impressive the car is.

The space, the tech, the drive, it’s magnificent. And it stays with you. We wanted to bottle that feeling and give it a rather dramatic expression. And so, this obsessive, paining young man yearning for another drive in his best mate’s new car was born.

And the result is this entertaining series of melodramatic films showing off the TIGGO 9’s best features.” Says Peter Stewart, GM Marketing, Chery Motors ANZ: “The TIGGO 9 has a habit of surprising people.

Its comfort, technology and refinement can genuinely change what you expect from a vehicle in this category. Rather than simply listing those features, we wanted to capture the feeling they leave you with once they’re gone.”
The campaign marks Chery’s first integrated campaign of 2026 and the latest chapter in its second year of partnership with Dentsu Creative.
Chery is principal sponsor of Nine’s The Block, with the TIGGO 9 television campaign running throughout the program’s 12-week season, supported by TV, BVOD, SVOD, OOH Digital, Social and Radio.

title: Gordon Legal gets personal in new brand campaign via By All Means
story: The campaign highlights the breadth of Gordon Legal’s work, from representing a gig economy worker injured on the road, to the pursuit of a global cruise behemoth over the White Island volcano disaster, through to representing hundreds of thousands Australians in the Robodebt class action resulting in the largest legal settlement in the nation’s history.

The stories, and the campaign, illustrate that behind every legal matter is a person whose life has been profoundly impacted – but no matter the size of the case: for Gordon Legal, the pursuit of justice is always personal.

Says Gordon Legal Senior Partner, Peter Gordon: “The matters we work on vary enormously in scale and complexity, but what unites them is the impact they have on real people and their families. “Many of our clients come to us at some of the most difficult moments in their lives.

While legal outcomes are incredibly important, our role is also to stand beside people throughout the process. This campaign reflects the commitment our lawyers bring to that responsibility every day.”

Says By All Means Co-Founder, Ed Howley: “No other law firm in Australia could make a campaign like this, because no other firm undertakes cases like these. From everyday personal injury through to some of the most complex legal matters ever pursued in this country.
But that’s not even the most remarkable part: we experienced first-hand, by interviewing the plaintiffs ourselves, that Gordon Legal’s staff are fully, totally and utterly invested in what they do.
It was evident that they care very deeply not only about the outcomes for their clients, but for society more broadly.”
Says By All Means Managing Partner, Georgie Pownall: “One of the most important tasks in conveying what a brand has to offer is mining for the truth, and then reflecting that in a meaningful way.

In this instance though, the truth was evident, and it’s telling that these incredible survivors were not only willing to share their stories with us, but were so eager to let others know how supported they felt through such a difficult time in their lives.”
Says Co-Founder, Toby Cummings: “This was a great test for BAMBOO, By All Means’ new production arm, to lift the bar on what a ‘testimonial’ film can be.

title: Royco asks what comes after ‘happily ever after’ in new Ada Apa Dengan Cinta campaign
summary: A popular marca de temperos da Unilever Indonésia, Royco, fez parceria com Ada Apa dengan Cinta, a mais...
story: Ada Apa Dengan Cinta, first released in 2002, became a defining cultural moment for Indonesian audiences, and the 2016 sequel Ada Apa Dengan Cinta 2 reunited the nation with Rangga and Cinta. But one question remained: what happened after the “happily ever after”?

Royco’s campaign, titled Bahasa Cinta Yang Beda (A Different Love Language), picks up that thread and explores how love can evolve over the course of a long relationship and find expression in everyday gestures rather than grand declarations.
At the centre of the campaign is a short film that showcases Cinta’s journey to understand Rangga’s love language and attempt to perfect an omelette – Rangga’s favourite dish – as an act of love.

The omelette becomes the campaign’s central symbol: a simple, everyday gesture that carries more meaning than any grand romantic declaration. Royco positions itself as part of that language – the ingredient in the small, daily moments where love quietly shows up.

This love story is brought to life by Royco in collaboration with frank. Singapore, Omnicom’s dedicated Unilever team, and director Teddy Soeria Atmadja – one of Indonesia’s most celebrated film directors, known for his work across cinema and Netflix productions.
The film stars Dian Sastrowardoyo and Sissy Prescillia, reprising their roles from the original franchise.

The creative idea draws on a cultural tension deeply familiar to Indonesian audiences: the gap between the aspirational Korean-drama romance they watch on television and the quieter, more real love of everyday life, and centres Royco as the brand that helps deepen connections through cooking.

Ilham Chairat Royco Masterbrand & Innovation Lead, Unilever, said: “Ada Apa Dengan Cinta has held a special place in Indonesian culture for over two decades as a story that generations of Indonesians have grown up with and returned to.

We are excited to extend the story into something new and relatable for audiences, by asking what love looks like when it becomes part of daily life without the heightened emotions of the teenaged years.

Royco has always believed that the kitchen is where love is expressed through the simple gesture of cooking for one another – and this campaign brings that belief to life in a way that feels meaningful to our audience.”

title: Havas Play taps gaming ad platform iion for new playable advertising offering across ANZ + APAC
story: A parceria fará com que a iion se torne a parceira tecnológica e plataforma exclusiva da Havas Play para construções jogáveis ​​e de minijogos, integrando seu Playable Creator Studio à oferta da Havas Play em toda a região.

A oferta, Havas Play:able, combinará a cultura e a experiência em entretenimento da agência com a tecnologia da iion para criar experiências de marca que incentivem o público a participar ativamente, em vez de visualizar passivamente um anúncio.

O lançamento reflete a abordagem Deliberadamente Diferente da Havas, ajudando as marcas a envolver o público por meio de experiências imersivas que confundem os limites entre conteúdo, entretenimento e comércio. Por meio do Playable Creator Studio da iion, a Havas Play será capaz de gerar conceitos e visualizações interativos personalizados e prontos para o pitch antes de passar para a produção e implantação.

A plataforma estará disponível em toda a rede Havas e diretamente para os clientes da marca. Vários clientes do Havas Play já estão explorando a capacidade de desenvolver uma série de experiências de jogos casuais nas categorias de varejo, FMCG e beleza.

O interesse inicial reflete a oportunidade de experiências de jogo simples e envolventes para conectar os consumidores com as marcas de novas maneiras, trazendo os princípios dos jogos para os ambientes físicos e digitais do dia a dia.
Diz Yun Yip, diretor comercial da iion: “A era da mídia passiva acabou – cada anúncio deve ser um convite para brincar, interagir e se envolver, porque é assim que o amor genuíno pela marca é criado.
A Havas Play compreende fundamentalmente a cultura e o entretenimento e, juntos, pretendemos levar o poder do “jogo” muito além dos jogos, para um ecossistema digital e social mais amplo.

“Ao fundir seu pulso cultural com nossa tecnologia, estamos transformando cada impressão em um momento ativo e de apoio que mantém as marcas na mente e, ao mesmo tempo, proporciona um desempenho mensurável em toda a experiência do jogador.”

Havas Play:able foi projetado para resolver algumas das barreiras tradicionais à publicidade jogável, que podem exigir custos iniciais de produção significativos e semanas de desenvolvimento antes que as marcas possam ver um conceito funcional.

A plataforma usa tecnologia de agente e automação de IA juntamente com estratégia criativa humana para desenvolver rapidamente visualizações interativas, permitindo que as marcas explorem conceitos jogáveis sem os requisitos iniciais de produção tradicionalmente associados ao formato.

story: Following a competitive tender, Travelex appointed Paper Moose as their creative and media agency to develop the new integrated ‘Reward Yourself’ campaign and bring the proposition to market.
The creative work tapped into the reality that travel can be unpredictable, silly, and unglamorous at times, which often become the best holiday memories.

Choosing striking visuals to maximum audience attention, these include a traveller coming face-to-face with a llama in Peru with the headline “Don’t just make friends with the locals. Reward yourself.”
The creatives were developed in a close collaboration, with Paper Moose delivering a fully-integrated service, across the creative, production and media.
The campaign uses out-of-home, supported by digital amplification at scale across programmatic and social media, as well as in-store signage and kiosk branding nationally.

Says Nick Hunter, CEO and ECD of Paper Moose: “Travelex is a global brand that understands what is happening in the world and shows up when it matters. We wanted to capture that energy. The work is bold, playful, and unapologetically human.”

Says Rob Dempsey, Head of Marketing, Australia and New Zealand at Travelex: “At its core, this partnership is about giving customers more value from every travel money purchase. It enables us to offer a benefit that resonates with customers and rewards them for something they’re already doing.

The campaign developed by Paper Moose captures that proposition in a bold and memorable way, creating a distinctive piece of work that stands out, helping us cut through in a highly competitive market.”

title: Spotify celebrates the power of music to transform everyday moments in new campaign
summary: Em um filme, um marido está se arrumando e arrumando o cabelo quando ouve sua esposa dizer “Aha!” do outro lado da sala....
story: These are scenes from “Roz ke kaam fun banao, Spotify Chalao”, Spotify’s new campaign built on a simple idea: music doesn’t just elevate life’s big moments, it transforms the everyday ones, too.
The campaign rolls out as a series of eight films across five languages – Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Bhojpuri.

Each film brings this idea to life in a different household setting – ironing clothes, washing dishes, fixing a lightbulb – where someone doing an everyday chore is visibly and joyfully transformed by music.
To the onlooker, it’s confusing, but to the person lost in the song, the chore is no longer simply a chore. The campaign’s premise resonates with how listeners already experience Spotify.

According to research, 97% of Indian users say Spotify makes mundane activities more enjoyable and makes everyday life better, 98% say Spotify is essential to their daily routine, and 71% say they feel relaxed when using the platform.

These findings reflect how music isn’t just background noise, but is actively changing how listeners experience their day. Shipra Srivastava, Head of Marketing, Spotify India, said: “There’s something universal about how music changes the texture of a moment.

It doesn’t matter what language you speak or what chore you’re doing, when the right song comes on, the task feels different. Cleaning the home, ironing clothes, washing utensils, fixing a light bulb – for millions of listeners, these are already music moments.

Our research backs this up – 98% of Indian users say Spotify is essential to their daily routine. This campaign is about that everyday relationship with music, and the joy it quietly adds to the routines we don’t think twice about.”

This everyday role is powered by a thriving and increasingly diverse music ecosystem. Spotify’s latest Loud & Clear report shows that listeners streamed Indian artists nearly 335 billion times on the platform in 2025, totaling over 20 billion hours of music.
And this listening is spreading across languages: royalties for Telugu artists grew over 120% year over year, while Malayalam rose over 30% and Tamil 20%, among other languages.

title: Domino’s asks Aussies+Kiwis to drop everything* in new campaign via Bureau of Everything
summary: EXCLUSIVO - A Domino's lançou hoje uma nova plataforma de marca via Bureau of Everything, oferecendo aos australianos e k...
story: Based on the undeniable truth that when that Domino’s box lands, everything else can wait. Drop Everything* It’s Domino’s™ was created to put one very important thing back at the centre of the Domino’s brand: craveability.

The launch is the culmination of the new partnership between Domino’s and Bureau of Everything, covering consumer research, a new brand strategy, design refresh, creative platform development, brand campaign and NPD launch.

Says Em Taylor, Strategy Founder at Bureau of Everything: “People told us that there are key moments when Domino’s wins, hands down. Because it’s the choice that truly pleases everyone, it crushes all the cravings in one order. Which in a world of overwhelming options makes it a clear fave.

We’ve built the strategy and platform around that truth.” Domino’s Head of Brand and Campaigns ANZ, Teneille Papp said the new platform has been designed to build a stronger and more distinctive Domino’s brand over the long term.
Says Papp: “In a market this crowded, cutting through takes a platform, not a campaign, built to flex across everything we do while staying unmistakably Domino’s.
Bolder, fresher, food creative so visceral it makes you want to lick the screen and a voice truly in on the joke, built to turn a transaction into a craving.”

The platform has been developed for the long term, and launches with a campaign that sets up the Drop Everything* It’s Domino’s™ idea in some pretty extreme circumstances. Which have resulted in some fun conversations with the legal department.

Says Cam Blackley, Creative Founder at Bureau of Everything: “There is an asterisk baked into the endline. It’s the creative wink from the brand that gives Domino’s permission to flex a more irreverent muscle in any moment or media channel.

Keeping the brand entertaining any time it shows up and theoretically indemnifying us against the overly literal that walk among us. Fingers crossed. “The asterisk isn’t the only distinctive asset in our arsenal.
There is also a new graphic design system that feels fresher and undeniably Domino’s; partnered with an editorial photography style that celebrates the mess and joy of nailing a slice.”

title: Australian Macadamias launches ‘You’ve Got Good Taste’ campaign via VOCAL
story: The campaign was born from new data commissioned by the brand to highlight Australia’s snacking behaviours.

The findings were striking: Australians continue to value quality when it comes to snacking, with four in five (79%) saying taste is their top priority when choosing a snack and more than 5.6 million Australians believing macadamias reflect good taste when entertaining.

Created by Weber Shandwick Australia in partnership with Australian Macadamias and Hort Innovation, You’ve Got Good Taste celebrates Australians who choose quality and flavour in the everyday, positioning Australian Macadamias as a simple signal of good taste.

Brought to life through a suite of video-led creative assets produced in partnership with Samsumo, the campaign playfully reminds consumers that when they choose Australian macadamias, they’re choosing one of Australia’s most distinctive snacks.
Says Ben Baldwin, CEO of Australian Macadamias: “You’ve Got Good Taste celebrates the Australians who appreciate quality in the everyday.

From entertaining at home to enjoying a simple snack, we’re shining a light on the small moments where good taste shows up and the role Australian macadamias can play in making those moments a little more special.”

“Australian macadamias are one of the country’s most premium homegrown products, and this campaign gives us a fresh, distinctive platform to ensure macadamias are top of mind when people are choosing a snack.”

The campaign will roll out nationally throughout September and October across social, digital, out-of-home and retail media, including activity across the Coles and Woolworths media networks, supported by paid media agency Benedictus.
It marks the next chapter in Australian Macadamias’ ongoing efforts to meet demand for and reinforce the premium credentials of Australian-grown macadamias within the domestic market.

title: KFC taps into pickle obsession with new ‘Picklecore’ brand campaign via Special
story: Created to launch its new KFC x Pickles limited-time offer (LTO), the campaign taps into Australia’s growing appetite for unconventional and polarising flavours, taking the current pickle obsession beyond food and positioning it as a lifestyle.

Special saw an opportunity to harness the enthusiasm of hardcore “pickle fanatics” and use it to draw the broader “pickle curious” into the cultural moment. Says Tom Martin, CCO & Partner at Special: “We didn’t just drop a menu item – we built an entire subculture.

By giving this LTO the high-fashion treatment it deserved, we turned a flavor obsession into full-blown Picklecore. It’s unapologetic, gloriously weird, and proves that when you lean into cultural absurdity, people don’t just eat the food – they live the lifestyle.”
Under the campaign platform, ‘It’s not a garnish.

It’s a lifestyle’, Picklecore gives the food trend the full high-fashion treatment, creating an exaggerated culture and identity around KFC’s new limited time only pickle range, including Pickle Burger, Pickle Pepsi Max, Frickles and Pickle Loaded Chips.

The campaign first appeared through teaser billboards featuring surreal Picklecore products including pickle pants, watches, and lipstick, before extending across social and culture with podcaster and radio host Luisa Dal Din.

At the centre of it is a 15-second hero film styled like a high-fashion campaign and soundtracked by techno, bringing the Picklecore world to life while deliberately blurring the lines between food advertising and fashion.
The film is supported by OOH, social, and audio executions, creating a multi-channel campaign designed to reach everyone from committed pickle fans to those yet to be converted.

Says Vanessa Rowed, CMO KFC SOPAC: “Continuing to push boundaries and lean into culture is at the heart of our success story. Picklecore is more than just a menu launch – it’s an invitation to our fans and the ‘pickle-curious’ to experience KFC in a totally new way.

“It shines a light on how we can take a passionate food obsession and turn it into bold, entertaining work, giving our biggest lovers of the brand an unmissable reason to drop in while driving real commercial momentum during a key period.”

title: Somersby launches ‘For a Night In-In’ campaign for Somersby Double (8.2%) via Clemenger BBDO
story: The fun, irreverent and somewhat quirky campaign departs from the traditional world usually associated with ciders – summer, meadows, and long afternoons – instead inserting the brand into the high-energy, early evening occasion.

Built from the simple insight that for many Gen Z and millennial drinkers the best part of their night is the bit before they head out, when they’re at home with their closest mates and they can truly be themselves. The launch campaign encourages consumers to lean into that occasion.

Says Amy Weston, Executive Creative Director, Clemenger BBDO: “Out-out always sounds like a good idea, until you’re standing in a queue at 2:00am. A night in-in is the sweet spot. Just mates, playlist privileges, and no plan. Somersby Double felt like the perfect partner for that-that.”
Somersby is Australia’s number 1 cider brand. It is owned by Carlsberg and distributed in Australia by Asahi.

With High-ABV Cider experiencing a period of extended growth and Gen Z drinkers progressively preferencing at-home drinking occasions, Somersby Double provides them with a new alternative, that shakes cider free from its old stereotypes without losing Somersby’s signature refreshing taste.

Says Sarah Wilcox, Asahi Beverages Head of RTDs and Cider: “With the strong growth we’re seeing in the high ABV cider segment, it’s exciting to see Somersby Double Apple 8.2% hitting shelves across Australia.

The ‘For a Night In-In’ campaign was inspired by a simple insight: some of the best moments of a night are often those first few drinks shared with friends. We wanted to celebrate those moments and encourage people to make them last a little longer by staying In Session.
It’s been incredibly rewarding to launch a product that expands the Somersby portfolio while staying true to the refreshing, fruity taste that has made Somersby Australia’s number one cider.”

Says Sidsel Marie Lyhne, International Marketing Manager, Carlsberg Export & License: “When a strong brand, clear category trend and a genuine consumer insight come together, that’s where the magic happens.
Somersby Double with its new campaign is the result of exactly that combination – brought to life through a fantastic collaboration between our teams and agency partners from the very beginning.

title: KIKO Milano presenta su nueva campaña global protagonizada por Madonna
story: Septiembre, 2026.- KIKO Milano , la marca de maquillaje número uno de Italia, revoluciona el mundo de la belleza global con el lanzamiento de su nueva campaña de marca y la presentación de su nueva Embajadora Global: Madonna, el máximo ícono de la autoexpresión y el estilo.
El lanzamiento cinematográfico de “The KIKO Show” invita al mundo a adentrarse en una nueva era a través de una provocadora pregunta: “¿Ya conoces KIKO?”

Fotografiada por el legendario fotógrafo Rafael Pavarotti, con dirección creativa de maquillaje a cargo de Marcelo Gutiérrez, Director Creativo Global de Maquillaje de KIKO Milano, y acompañada por un remix exclusivo de estreno mundial de Bring Your Love, el más reciente sencillo de Madonna, producido por el reconocido productor musical Stuart Price, la producción se presenta como un auténtico espectáculo teatral.
En ella, Madonna aparece frente a impactantes muros LED, transformándose en distintas personalidades de belleza, mientras transmite un mensaje contundente de empoderamiento. «Madonna es el referente.

Lo es todo» , afirmó Drew Elliott, Chief Brand Officer de KIKO Milano. «Trabajar con Madonna permitió llevar a KIKO Milano al siguiente nivel. La campaña fue diseñada para captar toda la atención, igual que nuestra musa y nuestros productos.

The KIKO Show apenas comienza y la marca aún tiene más sorpresas preparadas..» The KIKO Show presenta una historia de identidad, audacia y pasión. Más que una campaña, The KIKO Show es una muestra de la filosofía de KIKO Milano: ofrecer siempre lo mejor.

Impulsada por la convicción de que las mujeres inteligentes no pagan de más, la campaña destaca el compromiso de KIKO con la creación de fórmulas desarrolladas en Italia y productos inspirados en las tendencias más actuales y accesibles para todos.

Se trata de maquillaje para todos: calidad de alto desempeño sin sobreprecio. La campaña celebra una nueva etapa para la marca basada en la transformación. Madonna nos presenta a la mujer KIKO con una sencilla pregunta: “¿Ya conoces KIKO?”.
A partir de ese momento descubrimos quién es KIKO: la máxima representación de la italianidad. Es divertida. Es imposible de ignorar. Es italiana. Es global.

A medida que avanza la historia, las dramáticas siluetas envueltas en humo dan paso a intensos acercamientos que celebran el rico ADN italiano compartido entre Madonna y KIKO Milano. Ambos representan una actitud audaz y sin concesiones.

title: Americanas celebra 97 anos de história com campanha que une passado e futuro da marca
summary: Com mídia 360°, quatro lives comerciais e grandes ativações de retail media, companhia transforma aniversário em plataforma de conexão com consumidores e marcas parceiras Quase um século de história cabe […]
story: Com mídia 360°, quatro lives comerciais e grandes ativações de retail media, companhia transforma aniversário em plataforma de conexão com consumidores e marcas parceiras

Quase um século de história cabe em uma passadinha na loja antes do cinema, na busca pelo CD favorito ou na lembrança de uma compra que marcou uma geração. Em 2026, a Americanas comemora seus 97 anos e coloca no ar, nesta quarta-feira (9), sua campanha de aniversário, feita em parceria com a Suno.

Com o mote “Aniversário Americanas: ofertas históricas que todo mundo ama” , a campanha divertida combina nostalgia e ofertas para celebrar a relação construída com os brasileiros e, ao mesmo tempo, apresentar a Americanas que está sendo construída para os próximos 100 anos.

A campanha tem como protagonista o “Azinho” , ícone visual da marca que estreia como anfitrião da comemoração e se apresenta caracterizado de diversas gerações. A ideia é representar, de forma leve e afetiva, a evolução da companhia e sua presença na rotina de diferentes gerações.
A campanha terá mídia 360° , com presença em canais digitais, redes sociais, rádio, mídia exterior (DOOH) e televisão aberta. Os filmes serão veiculados na TV Globo a partir de hoje (09).

A estratégia inclui ainda quatro grandes lives comerciais , que combinam ofertas, entretenimento e interação com os consumidores. “Hoje, estamos construindo a Americanas que queremos ser nos nossos 100 anos.
Temos uma marca que faz parte da história dos brasileiros, geração após geração, e queremos preservar essa conexão, mas também renová-la.

A nossa transformação passa por entender melhor o consumidor, tornar sua experiência de compra mais completa e relevante e fazer com que a marca continue sendo um destino para diferentes momentos da vida dos nossos clientes”, afirma Aline de Oliveira , head de marketing da Americanas.
Aniversário impulsiona parcerias em formato de retail media Além de impulsionar as vendas, o aniversário se consolida como uma das principais campanhas de retail media da Americanas em 2026.

Por meio do Americanas Ads , grandes marcas parceiras ampliam sua presença nos ambientes físicos e digitais da companhia, combinando comunicação de marca, ofertas e diferentes pontos de contato com os consumidores.

title: Sapporo invites Aussies and New Zealanders to ‘Prepare for Fugu’ in new work via Sunday Gravy
story: Os consumidores que comprarem Sapporo podem participar do sorteio para ganhar uma experiência gastronômica de fugu no Japão, onde a infame iguaria é preparada apenas por chefs licenciados e altamente treinados. Para lançar a campanha, Sapporo lançou um curta-metragem inspirado em thrillers psicológicos japoneses.
O filme confunde a linha entre a realidade e a imaginação à medida que o medo do veneno começa a consumir todos os pensamentos, criando uma sensação crescente de tensão e desconforto.

O último capítulo de So Pour a Sapporo celebra o ritual de desaceleração, com uma das experiências mais únicas do Japão, melhor compartilhada com uma cerveja. Dizem Phoebe Joiner e Mary Graham, criativas sênior da Sunday Gravy: “A arte necessária para preparar o fugu é literalmente vida ou morte.
O ritual de comê-lo obriga você a estar presente. Queríamos capturar esse sentimento e, em seguida, dar aos australianos e aos neozelandeses a oportunidade de experimentá-lo por si próprios.”

Diz Amy Kearney, gerente de marketing da Sapporo Austrália/NZ: "So Pour a Sapporo celebra os momentos e as histórias que unem as pessoas tomando uma cerveja. Prepare for Fugu é outro convite para experimentar um lado do Japão que permanece com você por muito tempo depois que o copo está vazio."
A campanha integrada é lançada nacionalmente em filmes, cinema, OOH, PR, na embalagem, no local, digital, social e varejo.

title: Aussie expat Tara Ford leads Droga5 London’s reverse campaign for IKEA in Saudi Arabia
story: Ford moved to London in 2025 after leading The Monkeys and Droga5 Australia , taking the creative helm at Droga5 London. The new service acts as a step forward in IKEA Alsulaiman’s circular efforts and sustainability commitment.

With the brand’s new Buyback Service, customers sell their used IKEA furniture and IKEA buys it back. It’s shopping, in reverse. To launch it, every element of the campaign flips iconic IKEA assets. The BILLY bookcase, the famous STRANDMON yellow wing chair and other pieces are shown from behind.
From headlines to prices, everything is backwards. It’s a campaign designed to make people look twice.

The idea kicks off with a social teaser featuring the ‘DOG HOT,’ a backwards take on the brand’s iconic hot dog, accompanied by the message ‘IKEA goes reverse on September 6.’ The DOG HOT was created for the campaign teaser stunt using real IKEA buns and sausages.
The campaign marks Droga5 London’s first project for IKEA Alsulaiman and will run across social, digital, film, CRM, IKEA’s website and app, as well as in-store communication and other media.

Says Rami Rihani, Chief Marketing & Communications Officer at Alsulaiman Group: “The strongest ideas are often the simplest. IKEA’s Buyback Service reverses the traditional relationship between IKEA and our customers: they sell and we buy. We loved the idea of our ads doing the same.

It’s an idea that rewards people when they see it, using the familiarity of IKEA in an unexpected way. It’s been a great first project with Droga5 London, bringing a new perspective that complements the work we’re already doing and finding new ways to connect with our customers.”

Says Juliana Paracencio, Executive Creative Director at Droga5 London: “The idea was almost annoyingly simple. IKEA’s Buyback Service is shopping in reverse. So we reversed IKEA. The logo, the furniture, the copy, even the hot dog.

Once we landed the thought, the job was not getting in the way of it. The temptation is always to add more, but this idea was all about keeping things simple and pure.” Says Tara Ford, Chief Creative Officer at Droga5 London: “Iconic brand. Brilliant service. Bold and simple idea.

It’s a killer combination for any campaign.” The Dog Hot teaser launched on September 3rd, followed by the full Reverse Shop campaign on September 6th in Saudi Arabia. IKEA Alsulaiman is the official franchise holder for IKEA in Saudi Arabia and Bahrain.

title: BYRDLI launches creator-led travel commerce campaign with Alabama Tourism and Travel South USA
story: Rolling out across Australia and the United States, the campaign will see Australian photographer and videographer Ashley Dobson and acclaimed US photographer and videographer Terry McLauchlin travel through Alabama in opposite directions, each showcasing the state through their own perspective.

Through BYRDLI, the hotels, experiences, routes and itineraries they discover will become part of their own Travel Clubs, allowing audiences to move from seeing Alabama through someone they trust to exploring and booking travel inspired by the journey.
Dobson will travel from Huntsville to Mobile, experiencing Alabama for the first time and introducing the state to her Australian community.
McLauchlin will take the reverse route, travelling from Mobile to Huntsville and sharing Alabama with his US audience through the lens of one of the country’s highly regarded travel photographers.
Together, the journeys reveal a state where American music, Southern food, history, innovation and landscape intersect.

From Huntsville’s space and science story to communities shaped by music and civil rights history, local food traditions, Southern culture and the landscapes of Alabama’s south, the campaign is designed to showcase an America beyond the traditional gateways.
For Australian travellers in particular, Alabama offers many of the experiences they travel to the United States seeking, road trips, live music, culture, history, food and a genuine sense of place.

For Vanessa Richards, Co-Founder and CEO of BYRDLI, the campaign also demonstrates how creator-led destination marketing can move beyond awareness: “Travel creators have always been incredibly powerful at creating demand.

They influence the destination someone chooses, the hotel they stay in and the experiences they want to have. “What historically hasn’t existed is the infrastructure for that creator to remain part of the traveller’s journey when they’re ready to actually book.

“Ashley and Terry aren’t simply travelling through Alabama and creating content. They’re building bookable Alabama travel inside their own Travel Clubs, allowing their communities to move from inspiration to purchase. That is creator-led travel distribution and BYRDLI enabled that globally.”

title: Dog takes over Wellington waterfront as Footrot Flats lives on in new campaign for Water Safety New Zealand via These Guys I Know
story: Dog assumiu um abrigo de ônibus à beira-mar de Wellington esta semana, com uma colocação de grande formato de alto impacto no Oriental Parade marcando 50 anos de Footrot Flats e dando vida à parceria entre a Water Safety New Zealand e o lendário desenho animado da Nova Zelândia.

Legends Live On foi concebido como mais do que uma campanha única. A plataforma reúne mídia externa, conteúdo original, arrecadação de fundos e algumas das figuras criativas e culturais mais conhecidas da Nova Zelândia para celebrar o legado duradouro de Murray Ball e, ao mesmo tempo, apoiar a segurança da água.

No centro da iniciativa está uma peça particularmente rara da história cultural da Nova Zelândia: uma obra de arte original de Murray Ball, com um cão vestindo um colete salva-vidas, doada pela família Ball e agora sendo leiloada para arrecadar fundos para a Water Safety New Zealand.
A arte original foi acompanhada por uma edição limitada de apenas 50 impressões, restando apenas algumas depois de se tornar extremamente popular entre os fãs do Footrot Flats.
Uma linha de produtos de edição limitada com Dog também está disponível, com os lucros apoiando o trabalho da Water Safety New Zealand para evitar afogamentos.

A colocação em Wellington foi realizada em parceria com a oOh!media, com o abrigo de ônibus de grande formato e alto impacto na Oriental Parade colocando Dog na frente do tráfego de pedestres de alto valor, passageiros, banhistas e visitantes ao longo da icônica orla marítima da cidade.

A campanha também está sendo veiculada na rede de varejo da oOh!media, estendendo a presença do Legends Live On além da orla marítima e dando à plataforma uma presença mais ampla fora de casa, à medida que a Water Safety New Zealand busca doações para apoiar seu trabalho.

A localização da Parada Oriental foi deliberadamente selecionada pela sua forte ligação contextual com a campanha. Com a água visível atrás do abrigo do ônibus, o colete salva-vidas do Dog não é apenas parte da criatividade – o próprio ambiente reforça a mensagem.

O momento também é significativo, com a plataforma lançando na mesma semana que o projeto de lei de alteração dos coletes salva-vidas nas embarcações de recreio foi aprovado em terceira leitura no Parlamento.

Assim que a legislação entrar em vigor, todos a bordo de uma embarcação de recreio com seis metros ou menos de comprimento serão obrigados a usar um colete salva-vidas devidamente ajustado enquanto a embarcação estiver em movimento.

title: Jack Daniel’s brings back Gentleman Jack Dad Ads campaign via We Are Different + Starcom
story: For 2026, Gentleman Jack is taking the influencer platform further, drawing inspiration from the craftsmanship that defines the whiskey itself and recruiting dads and brand loyalists who have spent years learning, building and mastering crafts of their own.

Through a combination of user-generated and creator content, a series of social films uncovers the personal journeys behind each dad’s craft – pairing intimate interviews with throwback imagery documenting the years spent honing their skills.

Rather than treating casting, influencers and audiences as separate layers of the campaign, Dad Ads brings them into one connected social ecosystem. Brand fans become the creative starting point, creators bring their stories to life, and their communities help those stories travel.

The expanded campaign brings together creative, production, PR, social and influencer through We Are Different, with Starcom scaling Dad Ads beyond the social feed through an integrated paid media campaign spanning social and radio.

Says Ashleigh Buchner, Jack Daniel’s Brand Manager at Brown-Forman Australia: “Last year we made a deliberate choice to put influencer-led creative and authentic brand fans at the heart of our Gentleman Jack Father’s Day campaign.
This year, we’re doubling down on that approach, taking the idea beyond social and expanding it across digital and above-the-line media to build a bigger, more connected platform for Gentleman Jack.”
Says Stuart Terry, Founder and Director of We Are Different: “The first year of Dad Ads showed that some of a brand’s most powerful creative assets are the people and influencers who already love it.
This year, we found a fresh creative expression by bringing two kinds of craft together: the craftsmanship behind Gentleman Jack and the real-life crafts of the dads who love it.
By bringing brand fans, creators and communities together around that brand truth, we’re turning advocacy into an idea designed to earn attention in social and travel far beyond it.”

title: UTS College launches ‘The Year That Made Me’ genuine stories campaign via The Core Agency
summary: Rather than reconstructing that experience, The Year That Made Me tells genuine stories of how the momentum of UTS Colle...
story: The brief was to capture what actually changes for a student during their year at UTS College: growing confidence, a sense of belonging, and the resilience to keep going when things don’t go to plan, it was the year that made them the very best version of themselves.

Following the success of last year’s brand work for the University of Technology Sydney, UTS College opted to work with The Core Agency on their campaign, with the agency developing the strategic positioning and a creative campaign that cuts through the usual education sector wallpaper and appeals to social media natives.
Rather than reconstructing that experience, The Year That Made Me tells genuine stories of how the momentum of UTS College helped real students create their identities.
A suite of films and digital assets were crafted from authentic student content from their year at the College, so the story of that growth is told in their own words.

Says Christian Finucane, Creative Director and Founder, The Core Agency: “Gen Z see straight through marketing hype, so we knew the best way to convince them was to be real and feature the people who had already been to UTS College and killed it.”

Adds Natasha Wheeler, Brand and Communication, UTS College: “It’s easy for this sector to talk in outcomes, degrees, pathways, results. What matters to our students is the belonging and transformation they build along the way, and we wanted this campaign to reflect that.
The Core Agency brought that vision to life, and we’re so proud of how our students are celebrated in it.”

Says Nikki Duffey, Campaign and Digital, UTS College: “It was important that this campaign still felt like UTS College, reflecting the University’s brand while giving our own creative and personality room to come through.

That balance is what made the stories feel true to our students,” says Nikki Duffey, Campaign and Digital, UTS College. Adds Finucane: “Through their stories we quickly discovered the immensely positive impact UTS College had on students.

It was a lot of fun and a great privilege to work on a product that genuinely gives people more confidence and changes their futures.” The campaign launches across paid social, digital video, owned assets and student touchpoints. Full name (required). Pseudonyms no longer accepted.

title: Michael Caton and NRL Hall of Famer Steve Menzies star in new campaign for VoltX Energy
story: The campaign is a multi-agency initiative involving Tiny Giants, Sweeney Advertising, Manly Warringah Sea Eagles, In The Media PR alongside the VoltX Energy marketing team.
The three 30 second advertisements use humour and nature documentary satire to drive a simple message – solar panels without the batteries are only half the solution.

The campaign follows neighbours Caton and Menzies through Menzie’s absurd attempts to reduce his electricity bills – first he forces Manly Sea Eagles players to pedal exercise bikes as generators (which fails when they tire and his wife needs to use the oven), then Caton adopts a David Attenborough style narration while observing Menzies’ incomplete solar panel solution through binoculars,…
The series then culminates with Caton crashing a ‘Bill Shock Support Group’ just for the meat pies, revealing his VoltX battery has freed him from bill anxiety and gives hope to his neighbour.

Says Caton: “Before I was an actor I was selling windmills so I love the idea of nature helping both us and the planet which is why I jumped at the chance to have some fun to create awareness around home batteries and bill shock that’s so topical right now.

“My own power bill had doubled in less than 12 months so I really needed a battery to wipe out my power bills, it surprised me how long the battery power lasts despite all the home appliances running.

“I actually thought I was too old to get a home battery but now having one I’m addicted to watching the app to see how much power is in my battery. It’s become a bit of a competition with myself to see how much I can generate compared to how much I’m using.”

The veteran actor first gained attention in the 70’s hit TV show The Sullivans before making his way into the hearts of Australians in the late 90’s film The Castle and was nominated for a Logie for his role in Packed to the Rafters.
Both Caton and Menzies believe increased awareness of battery technology will be crucial as Australia continues to face increasing electricity prices and looks to make better use of solar power.
Says Menzies: “Most people just accept they still have a power bill, even with solar, not realising they could have no bills or even be making money from the grid with a battery.”

title: Duolingo brings English learning to Punjabi speakers in new campaign via Talented
summary: Duolingo, a plataforma de aprendizagem móvel líder mundial, lançou seu novo programa ‘Aprenda Inglês com PunjabiR...
story: Spoken by more than 100 million people worldwide, Punjabi is among the most widely spoken languages globally, with vibrant communities across India, Canada, the United Kingdom, the United States and Australia. Written in Gurumukhi script, Punjabi carries a rich literary and cultural heritage.
The new course enables Punjabi speakers to begin their English learning journey from Gurumukhi, helping them access education, career opportunities and connections around the world.

This campaign, created by Talented & Calm Kaam, marks Duolingo’s second regional language course for North India after Hindi. Punjabi now joins its growing portfolio of regional courses, alongside Hindi, Bengali, Telugu and Tamil.
“Being able to launch this course in my mother tongue is incredibly meaningful and a moment of real pride for me,” said Karandeep Singh Kapany, Regional Marketing Director, India and South East Asia.

“Punjabis have long embraced opportunities beyond borders, pursuing education, careers and new beginnings around the world. By making English learning available in Punjabi, we’re helping remove language barriers and enabling even more people to access the opportunities that English can unlock.
This launch reflects our commitment to making high-quality education more accessible, inclusive and relevant for learners across South Asia and beyond.”
To bring the course to life, Talented looked beyond simply translating the proposition into Punjabi and instead rooted the campaign in the culture, humour and language of the region.
At the centre of it is Ullu Da Pattha, a phrase deeply woven into Punjabi vernacular and typically used playfully to call someone a fool or a mischief-maker.

The campaign reclaims a phrase that often begins as a casual reprimand from parents and elders and turns it into something you can aspire to become. What was once something you were called out for becomes a badge of sorts, with Duolingo turning it into a creative device for its entry into Punjab.

The films, produced by Bushra Shariff’s Calm Kaam, build on this spirit, bringing the proposition into distinctly Punjabi worlds and letting the culture, humour and absurdity of those situations drive the storytelling.

title: Muma Malaysia puts human craft at the heart of ONE Asia 2026 ‘Where Taste Matters’ campaign
summary: O ONE Asia 2026 do One Club for Creativity está entrando em sua chamada final de inscrições, com prazo final definido para setembro...
story: The judging will take place at The Majestic Kuala Lumpur, with DirectorThinkTank as exclusive judging sponsor, followed by a student masterclass with Level Up on October 20.
For its 2026 call-for-entry campaign, Muma Malaysia has put the spotlight firmly on human creativity with “Where Taste Matters” – a campaign built entirely by hand and without AI.

The idea explores the role of human taste in an increasingly AI-driven creative landscape, where content can be generated at unprecedented scale but instinct, experience and judgment remain difficult to replicate.

Rather than position the campaign as an anti-AI statement, Muma says it is a celebration of human intuition and the craft behind great creative work. “Artificial Intelligence was on every feed, every news platform, and everyone’s mind,” said Muma Malaysia.
“In an AI-driven world where creativity is endlessly generated, human taste matters more than ever. ‘Taste’ has become one of the most valuable currencies that AI cannot replicate.”

The agency developed a visual identity in which the word TASTE becomes the hero, experimenting over two months with different materials, handcraft techniques and organic textures. The team bleached cloth, weaved paper strips and even lit hundreds of matches to create the campaign imagery.
“We made it a point not to use any AI tools to produce the work,” said Muma. “Not because we were against AI, but because we wanted to champion the beauty of imperfection in human craft.”
The campaign is designed to resonate across APAC, drawing on the region’s diverse cultures, stories, humour and perspectives as expressions of taste.
For Muma, the process itself became part of the message – experimenting, failing, adjusting and trusting instinct rather than searching for a perfect answer.

The agency says the campaign reflects what it believes ONE Asia represents: a platform for creatives who continue to question, craft and exercise judgment in deciding what constitutes great work. The ONE Asia 2026 final entry deadline is September 18, 2026. Full name (required).

title: NexGard SPECTRA turns the media schedule into a monthly reminder in new campaign via OMD New Zealand and Good Gravy
story: A OMD Nova Zelândia desenvolveu uma estratégia que prioriza a mídia que concentra a atividade acima da linha do NexGard Spectra nos dias que antecedem o primeiro dia de cada mês, transformando a própria programação da mídia em um lembrete recorrente projetado para ajudar os donos de animais de estimação Kiwi a construir um hábito duradouro de proteção aos animais de estimação.

A primeira fase da campanha foi lançada antes de primeiro de setembro, com criativos desenvolvidos pela Good Gravy apresentando os embaixadores da marca de longa data, Colin e sua mãe, Dame Lisa Carrington.

Diz Richard Duckworth, chefe de animais de companhia da Boehringer Ingelheim Nova Zelândia, empresa controladora da NexGard Spectra: “Cães e gatos de estimação na Nova Zelândia são cada vez mais considerados membros da família.

Com a ajuda de veterinários e outros profissionais de saúde animal, os donos de animais de estimação compreendem melhor do que nunca que manter os seus animais de estimação protegidos contra parasitas também ajuda a manter as suas famílias protegidas, porque alguns destes insectos podem ser transferidos de animais de estimação para humanos.

Os donos de animais de estimação nos disseram que desejam tratar regularmente, mas às vezes esquecem e precisam de um lembrete. Trabalhando com a OMD e a Good Gravy, percebemos que a nossa publicidade poderia ser esse lembrete.“

Apresentada em vídeos on-line, sites de notícias, mídias sociais e fora de casa, a campanha combina uma presença mensal concentrada na mídia com os rostos familiares de Colin e Dame Lisa, enquanto posicionamentos interativos inteligentes permitem que os donos de animais de estimação adicionem datas futuras de tratamento diretamente em seus calendários.

Diz Keri Brown, Diretora de Negócios da OMD Nova Zelândia: "A criação de hábitos depende muito de sistemas e processos, mais do que de metas. Ao reformular esta campanha em torno da construção de um hábito nacional entre os donos de animais de estimação Kiwi, identificamos uma oportunidade de usar a mídia de forma diferente.

Trabalhando ao lado da Good Gravy, demos vida a esse pensamento por meio de um sistema de lembretes mensais simples e memorável.” Diz Lina Montero Soto, Diretora e Estrategista de Comunicação da Good Gravy: “A estratégia e a visão da OMD deram-nos o trampolim perfeito.

Quando o próprio plano de mídia se torna um lembrete, o salto criativo é fácil. Com Dame Lisa e Colin, o cavoodle, à frente, transformamos um trabalho fácil de esquecer em um hábito fácil de manter. Esse é o trabalho que amamos, criativo que resolve um problema cotidiano dos donos de animais de estimação.”

title: News24 unveils first campaign since Sky News Australia rebrand via Today The Brave + Roller
story: Drawing on the editorial heritage and credentials of News Corp’s global brand identity, News24 reflects the transformation of Australia’s first 24-hour TV news channel into a globally ambitious digital-first news brand.

The landmark rebrand campaign is the network’s most significant marketing initiative to date designed to reinforce its connection with loyal viewers, readers and listeners while expanding its reach among news-engaged audiences.

Independent media agency Kaimera led the media strategy and planning to deliver a fully integrated roll-out across TV, digital, print, PR, social, audio, out-of-home, transit, and retail to maximise reach, impact and audience engagement.

Emma Van Der Aa, News24’s Head of Marketing and Communications, said the campaign was carefully created to retain audience trust while modernising and repositioning the news brand for future growth: “Renaming a trusted news network built on three decades of brand equity presented a unique challenge but also a rare opportunity to build upon a proud legacy of journalism.

To seamlessly transition our loyal audience of 11.3 million monthly Australians to our new name without losing the connection we’ve built over decades, our strategy focused on talent-led creative across major touchpoints to reinforce our core brand proposition of real news and honest views.
“We’re just over a month in and the audience results are encouraging, supporting both our creative approach and media strategy, with strong engagement across our multiplatform network.”

At the centre of the campaign is a new visual identity built from the ground up in partnership with Foxtel’s creative agency Balboa, including a new logo, refreshed motion graphics package and redesigned studio environment to create a distinctive and contemporary brand presence across every platform.

Jessica Burton, Head of Creative at News24, said the rebrand provided a rare opportunity to rethink every visual element of the network’s signature design, including the commissioning of a new theme track with the acclaimed team at Uncanny Valley: “For us, this was far more than a renaming project.
We approached it as the creation of an entirely new brand identity, developing a distinctive visual system that reflects the scale of News24’s ambition and positions us for the future.

“From our broadcast studios and show branding through to our motion design, and new network theme song and sonic, every element was purpose-built to create a cohesive and recognisable audience experience that is distinctly News24.”

title: Airbag Man launches new brand campaign ‘Feel the Performance’ via New Word Order
story: The campaign is built to do something a spec sheet never could: make people feel the difference that air suspension makes, long before they ever get behind the wheel.
New Word Order partner Scott Oxford said the campaign puts drivers in the discomfort of an unsupported ride: “You can’t sell a feeling with facts.
“Airbag Man’s core audience – tourers, tradies and weekend 4×4 warriors – already knows their vehicles intimately, and many already have their product installed.

“This campaign extends to a new audience – new 4×4 drivers and caravan owners – who can quickly understand the product benefits for their comfort and safety. “To help them do this, this campaign makes them physically feel the problem first, then resolve it the moment Airbag Man enters the picture.

“It gives the brand a sensory hook that can flex across every future product range and campaign.” Airbag Man has spent close to two decades engineering air suspension systems and is a market leader locally and in its export markets.

Until now, the brand had never told its own story with the same confidence it builds its products. Feel the Performance is NWO’s first full campaign for ABM, built on a brief to help a sceptical, experienced audience not just understand what air suspension does, but feel exactly what it means.
Says Oxford: “Air suspension is experienced through the body – in the driver’s seat, in the stomach, in the shudder through the steering wheel – long before it’s understood as a product benefit.

“Rather than lead with technical performance claims, every execution is built on the same problem/solution architecture. “It heightens the discomfort, chaos and unpredictability of driving unsupported, then resolves it completely the moment Airbag Man enters the picture.”
So a bobblehead shudders violently on a corrugated dirt road, and kids brace in the back seat. But with suspension, the ride on the same road is smooth, level and controlled.
Developed as a scalable content suite from a single hero shoot, the Feel the Performance campaign is running across BVOD, radio and digital display.

title: IKEA Hong Kong makes room for what matters in new campaign via TBWA\Hong Kong
summary: A TBWA\Hong Kong criou a sua primeira campanha no âmbito da sua nova parceria com a IKEA Hong Kong, na sequência de uma competição...
story: It’s an understanding that counts for more in a category increasingly defined by aggressive price wars amid growing competition from the mainland, and one IKEA is using to reframe the narrative with this new campaign.
Rather than competing on cost alone, the brand speaks directly to the lived reality of Hong Kong homes and the Hong Kong spirit.
With IKEA’s storage and organisation solutions, Hong Kongers can make the most of every famously squeezed square foot – even the tiniest flat can fit everything that matters.

“IKEA has long been part of the story of Hong Kong homes, but this campaign marks a new chapter”, said Julia Shen, Marketing Manager. “TBWA\Hong Kong brought a level of cultural intelligence that helped us shape a communication platform celebrating how Hong Kongers live.
This campaign speaks to what matters most to our customers: the freedom to make their homes deeply personal, to fill them with the things they love – no matter how small the space.”

“Make Space For What You Love” brings Hong Kong culture to life through four distinct narratives, each paired with an iconic IKEA storage and organisation solution: TROFAST (“Fits Hong Kong People’s Cleverness”) celebrates the resourcefulness and ingenuity that defines Hong Kong people, PAX (“Fits Hong Kong People’s Annual Leave”) speaks to the escape and personal space every Hong Konger…
The campaign tells these four stories via a 20-second TVC that captures the emotional heart of the message through striking visuals blending IKEA’s wit with authentic Hong Kong insights.

These same visuals appear across the city’s most iconic locations, from Island Beverley to major transport hubs including MTR 12-sheet displays and a media takeover at Mei Foo Station, as well as across buses throughout Hong Kong – alongside integrated social and digital experiences.

“Storage is the most emotional product in the home, yet the category has never treated it that way,” said William Chow, Creative Partner at TBWA\Hong Kong. “Everyone sells capacity, because capacity is easy to measure.

But nobody keeps things because they have space, they keep things because they can’t let go. That emotional attachment is what elevated a product campaign into a brand one. We stopped selling what IKEA fits inside a cabinet and started showing what IKEA holds for seven million people.”

title: Olla & Uber te ajudam a chegar lá
summary: Criadora do Dia do Sexo, a Olla leva a data para a mobilidade e o delivery com descontos em corridas da Uber e ofertas no iFood, sempre lembrando o uso de preservativo.
story: Olla leva ações do Dia do Sexo para Uber e iFood, com descontos ligados à data (Crédito: Divulgação) A Olla firmou ações com Uber e iFood para o Dia do Sexo, celebrado neste domingo, 6 de setembro.
A data foi criada pela própria marca em 2008 como uma iniciativa publicitária e passou a integrar seu calendário de comunicação. Na Uber, consumidores poderão obter R$ 6,90 de desconto em corridas.

A parceria, que adota o mote “No dia 06/09, Olla & Uber te ajudam a chegar lá”, também prevê mensagens de conscientização sobre o uso de preservativos dentro da plataforma. No iFood, a companhia oferecerá descontos de até 69% em produtos Olla.
A estratégia de comércio rápido inclui ainda entregas em até dez minutos por meio de plataformas como iFood, Daki e Rappi.
“Queremos estar presentes de maneira relevante nos momentos em que as pessoas vivem suas relações, trazendo a proteção para a conversa de um jeito que dialogue com os hábitos de hoje.
No Dia do Sexo, aproveitamos para reforçar essa mensagem e estimular escolhas mais conscientes”, afirma Bruna Nobre, gerente de marketing de Intimate Wellness e Personal Care da Reckitt Comercial.

title: StarHub gets more from 5G+ with integrated campaign from TBWA\Singapore
story: Lançada em 25 de agosto, a campanha usa os cativantes Hublings da StarHub, que personificam o compromisso da marca com confiabilidade e cobertura.

Os personagens se unem para formar a 5ª barra de rede – uma expressão visual da conexão mais forte que os consumidores podem esperar do 5G+ – enquanto carregam um sinal “+” enorme em cenários do mundo real.

Desde estacionamentos subterrâneos e supermercados até praças de alimentação e muito mais, os locais trazem a promessa de capacidade expandida e de como os clientes podem estar mais conectados ao que importa onde quer que estejam.

As aquisições dinâmicas de transporte público em ônibus e MRT estendem a mensagem “Obtenha mais” aos principais locais de Cingapura, colocando a campanha em movimento e trazendo-a para as jornadas diárias dos consumidores.

Mas a campanha vai além da conscientização, dando vida ao “Get More with 5G+” no Lau Pa Sat por meio de uma ativação enraizada em uma verdade muito cingapuriana: quando se trata das coisas que amamos, sempre há espaço para mais.
No dia 2 de setembro, o StarHub assumiu a hora do almoço no icônico destino dos vendedores ambulantes, oferecendo aos clientes mais do que desejam, com sorvete grátis ilimitado das 11h30 às 15h00.

O comedor competitivo e criador de conteúdo Zermatt Neo também deu início à experiência colocando a ideia de “mais” à prova definitiva em seu próprio desafio alimentar na hora do almoço, mostrando até onde os cingapurianos podem ir quando há mais no menu.

O “mais” estendeu-se para além da mesa e para as ruas, com os Hublings do StarHub formando uma multidão de guarda-chuvas em torno de Lau Pa Sat para oferecer aos pedestres a sombra necessária do calor do meio-dia de Cingapura.

Uma literalização lúdica de “Mais cobertura”, a façanha transformou um benefício do 5G+ em algo que as pessoas pudessem ver e experimentar por si mesmas. Juntas, a ativação dá vida ao espírito “Obtenha mais com 5G+” de maneiras distintamente cingapurianas.

Peter Callaghan, Diretor Criativo do Grupo, TBWA\Singapura, disse: "'Obtenha mais com 5G+' tem tudo a ver com oferecer mais às pessoas. Mais velocidade, mais cobertura, mais daquilo que elas realmente desejam.

title: PlayStation New Zealand turns local chippy into nostalgic activation via Eleven PR NZ
story: Trocando takeaways por takedowns, o chippy funcional foi equipado com duas máquinas de fliperama especializadas personalizadas pela V3, além de embalagens de alimentos nostálgicas, formulários de pedidos personalizados, pôsteres de personagens e mercadorias exclusivas do evento.

A ideia aproveitou a nostalgia compartilhada dos jogos de luta dos anos 90: colocar uma moeda para chamar sua casa, aglomerar-se em volta do armário, observar o campeão em título e esperar pela sua vez – tudo isso enquanto espera pelo seu peixe com batatas fritas em uma noite de sexta-feira.

Eleven PR reuniu uma lista de convidados de mídia, criadores, artistas e membros da comunidade de jogos de Aotearoa que passaram por sessões de jogo dedicadas, enfrentando peixe e batatas fritas antes que a noite continuasse no vizinho RSC.

Krister Robinson, chefe de marketing da PlayStation Nova Zelândia, diz que a equipe queria criar um lançamento local que capturasse a energia competitiva e a experiência social no coração dos jogos de luta.

"Os melhores lançamentos locais encontram uma maneira de pegar um lançamento global e torná-lo genuinamente relevante para o mercado. Para nós, encher uma loja local de peixe e batatas fritas com máquinas de fliperama personalizadas reuniu a nostalgia e a energia competitiva do jogo com algo que parecia distintamente Kiwi."

A PlayStation NZ trabalhou com a Eleven PR para desenvolver o conceito de lançamento local e liderar a mídia, o criador e a estratégia conquistada da campanha, com V3 supervisionando a produção e a construção de arcade especial.

Eleisha Balmer, Client Partner da Eleven PR, diz que criar uma experiência da qual as pessoas desejam fazer parte nem sempre requer uma ideia ou produção excessivamente complicada: “Às vezes, trata-se de encontrar uma conexão cultural simples e se comprometer com ela.

Havia algo divertido e familiar em ter um jogo de arcade no bairro chippy, é quase tão icônico quanto aquele pôster icônico com todos os peixes. “Sabíamos que ele havia pousado quando as pessoas começaram a perguntar se as máquinas poderiam ficar.

Houve mais do que alguns pedidos para fazer do Nate’s Plaice um fliperama permanentemente!” A ativação atraiu 50 convidados e gerou 71 coberturas sociais nas primeiras 24 horas, com alcance potencial de mais de 1,79 milhão. Nome completo (obrigatório).

title: Macca’s invites Aotearoa to celebrate its 50th birthday in new campaign via McCann NZ
story: Todos sabemos que os Kiwis adoram marcar uma ocasião, por isso a Macca’s New Zealand, a McCann New Zealand e a OMD estão a fazer exactamente isso. Juntos, eles estão lançando uma campanha ambiciosa para marcar cinco décadas desde que sua primeira loja na Nova Zelândia abriu em Porirua, em 1976.
Em vez de um aniversário tradicional da marca, a campanha coloca os clientes no centro da celebração, com personagens icónicas da Macca, jogos, prémios e muitos motivos para se juntar à celebração.

No centro das celebrações estão três personagens de Macca: Birdie the Early Bird, Grimace e Hamburglar. O trio assumiu o trabalho muito sério de ajudar o Macca’s a comemorar sua quinta década – com tanto caos e diversão quanto você esperaria.

Os clientes podem ganhar um bônus de aniversário ao comprar um pacote de aniversário, digitalizando um código QR para escolher entre 35% de desconto em brinquedos online no The Warehouse ou 30 minutos de jogo grátis no Timezone. Também há mais chances de ganhar por meio do aplicativo McDonald’s.

Os clientes que encomendam itens com ingressos selecionados recebem ‘jogadas’ que desbloqueiam jogos de aniversário, com uma chance em 3 de ganhar comida grátis, incluindo favoritos como Big Mac ou McChicken.

O diretor de criação da McCann Nova Zelândia, Gary Steele, diz que a campanha foi projetada para capturar a diversão irreverente de uma grande festa: "Pensamos que se você vai comemorar 50 anos, é melhor fazê-lo corretamente. "Queríamos que o trabalho parecesse uma celebração de aniversário, não um aniversário corporativo.
É tudo uma questão de participação – dar aos Kiwis muitas razões para se envolverem, divertirem-se e, idealmente, ganharem uma ou duas guloseimas ao longo do caminho.”

O chefe de marca e mídia do McDonald’s da Nova Zelândia, Leigh Benvie, disse que a campanha reflete a conexão da marca com seus clientes: “Não se trata de celebrarmos a nós mesmos – trata-se de celebrar nossos clientes e o que o Macca’s significou em suas vidas nas últimas cinco décadas.
"Víamos os 50 anos como a desculpa perfeita para reunir todos e nos divertir. Porque quando se completa 50 anos, quanto mais, melhor."

Com lançamento em 2 de setembro, a celebração de seis semanas abrange TVC, OLV, digital, OOH, social e PR, com cada elemento projetado para dar vida aos 50 grandes e incentivar os clientes de Aotearoa a se envolverem.

title: NRMA Roadside Assistance turns cultural intelligence into new ‘Every Trip Matters’ campaign via CulturalPulse
story: Analysis of NRMA’s 3.6 million-strong membership base using CulturalPulse’s AskGenie audience intelligence technology found Chinese and Indian Australian drivers to be significantly under-represented in comparison to the diverse NSW/ACT general population, despite these communities having very high car dependency.

Every Trip Matters is NRMA Roadside Assistance’s first in-language campaign, with story-led creative in English, Hindi, Punjabi, Mandarin and Cantonese featuring real families and community members rather than actors.

The integrated campaign spans cultural media and community distribution, dedicated in-language landing pages, a three-month free membership offer and in-community education sessions with NRMA Technicians.
CulturalPulse’s community brand ambassadors have been instrumental in shaping the work and will drive its rollout through trusted networks across Chinese and Indian Australian communities.

NRMA Roadside General Manager of Marketing and Proposition, Kate McBean says: “We believe there was an opportunity to better connect with Chinese and Indian Australian communities, but we also recognise that reaching them effectively meant doing things differently.

“The NRMA wants to understand the experiences of these communities that we hope to represent and serve, the role their cars play in everyday life and what would make Roadside Assistance relevant to them.

Simply taking our existing marketing campaigns and translating them into other languages is not how we want to show up for your community.” “Every Trip Matters reflects that thinking. We want every Australian to feel that NRMA Roadside Assistance is there for them, wherever they go.”

The work marks the first campaign partnership between CulturalPulse and NRMA Roadside Assistance. Rohan Nayee, Head of Client Service at CulturalPulse, says: “The campaign demonstrates why reaching multicultural Australia requires more than an in-language execution.

“Language matters, but translation alone doesn’t build relevance. You need to understand the audience first, then carry that understanding through the creative, the media, the customer experience and how you show up in the community. “That’s what we’ve built with NRMA.

The stories come from real community experiences, feature real community members and will be delivered through the channels and networks they know and trust. “When all of those pieces work together, you’re not simply reaching an audience.

title: Club 4X4 Insurance introduces Bob the Bobblehead in new campaign via The Reactor
story: Club 4X4 Insurance is uniquely tailored for 4WD enthusiasts who take their vehicles on off-road adventures. They offer coverage anywhere you can legally drive in Australia, alongside separate agreed value cover for modifications and built-in vehicle recovery.

While the brand was originally built on a strong foundation of word-of-mouth within the 4WD community, The Reactor’s previous work drove significant growth in both brand awareness and new policy uptake. This year’s campaign aims to accelerate that momentum by adding to their suite of brand assets.

The Reactor’s Creative Director, Nick Brown, says collaborating with the Club 4X4 marketing team is an absolute joy: “They are strategy-first, with a deep understanding of the power of brand and where awareness versus tactical messaging should sit in the funnel,” Brown explains.
“Their challenge to us was to develop a mascot that embodied the ‘Free the 4WD’ sentiment of the brand, but could also be playful and fun, as the brand doesn’t want to take itself too seriously.”

Tom King, Brand Marketing Manager for Club 4X4, notes that the brand faces a unique hurdle in the highly competitive insurance sector: “We’re in a fortunate position where we have a really compelling offer for 4WDers compared to our competitors, but we don’t have their budgets, so any campaign we bring to market needs to be recognisable.

“We knew we needed to add more distinctiveness to Club 4X4’s brand, so when The Reactor came to us with Bob, we could see its strength immediately. The nodding head embodies our role in our customers’ lives, being an enabler to their lifestyle rather than a blocker.

We’re very happy with how The Reactor executed the idea, bringing the reality of boring work video calls to life and capturing a moment we all want to break free from in our daily lives.” The new campaign is live across TV, OOH, and digital platforms from the end of August.

title: One New Zealand wants Kiwis to pick up the phone in new ‘Misinterpreted’ campaign via McCann
story: Confrontado com a mudança das normas sociais e as divisões geracionais – com pesquisas mostrando que 25% das pessoas entre 18 e 34 anos nunca atendem o telefone, 70% preferem mensagens de texto e 81% ficam ansiosos ao ligar – McCann aproveitou a oportunidade para convidar os Kiwis a redescobrirem o valor de uma chamada telefónica tradicional.

O criativo da campanha destaca os textos, emojis e frases que usamos todos os dias, expondo os significados totalmente diferentes que eles podem carregar: desde um polegar para cima sem enfeites ou um 'k' brutal, até o confuso 'tudo bem se não' ou 'morrendo' geracionalmente divisivo (eles precisam de uma ambulância ou você acabou de contar uma ótima piada?).

Ganhando vida através de simples OOH e execuções impressas, ‘Mal interpretado’ dá vida a uma verdade simples: o tom e o contexto podem ser perdidos em uma mensagem, por isso muitas vezes ficamos na dúvida. Mas você sempre sabe com uma ligação.

Alan Jones e Angelo An, Diretor Criativo do Grupo da McCann Nova Zelândia, afirmam: “As mensagens são um campo minado. A força desta campanha é que todos nós já passamos por isso e todos têm seus próprios exemplos. Pensar que alguém está com raiva quando não está. Pensar que alguém não está com raiva quando está.
Ou aprender que seu emoji de polegar para cima está aterrorizando seus colegas de trabalho mais jovens. Sim… é melhor apenas ligar.”

Georgia Mahaffie, gerente geral de marca e marketing da One New Zealand, diz que a campanha envolvente é construída sobre uma verdade humana universalmente identificável que se liga perfeitamente à mensagem central da marca.

“Todos nós olhamos para uma mensagem de texto e pensamos: ‘O que isso significa?’ E, aparentemente, até mesmo um sinal de positivo pode causar problemas hoje em dia.” “É isso que adoro neste trabalho.

É simples, é atual e mostra o que quero dizer sem se levar muito a sério. ‘Let’s Get Connected’ tem como objetivo principal unir as pessoas – e às vezes a melhor maneira de fazer isso ainda é simplesmente pegar o telefone.” A campanha foi lançada em 24 de agosto e é veiculada em OOH e impressão.

title: Strength Baked In
summary: A Hovis investe 4 milhões de libras em uma campanha multicanal que resgata os antigos letreiros pintados da marca em fachadas pelo Reino Unido para reforçar sua herança.
story: A Hovis está lançando uma grande campanha multicanal nacional de £ 4 milhões, ‘Strength Baked In’, que ocorrerá até setembro, outubro e novembro. Isto marca a primeira atividade de marketing desde a aquisição da marca pela Associated British Foods (ABF) em julho.
A campanha apresenta um anúncio em vídeo de 30 segundos que visa mostrar a Hovis como uma das marcas mais populares da Grã-Bretanha e reforça a longa história comercial da empresa no Reino Unido.

O vídeo mostra anúncios antigos (o fantasma de Hovis canta) pintados em edifícios em todo o Reino Unido como parte de uma narrativa criativa mais ampla que conecta a empresa às comunidades locais. Hovis estimou que a atividade de marketing atingirá 79% dos principais compradores domésticos em canais de TV e mídia.

A campanha será apoiada por publicidade multicanal na TV, vídeo sob demanda, fora de casa, rádio e mídias sociais. Além disso, a empresa está preparada para lançar relações públicas para o consumidor e mídia de varejo. Inscreva-se aqui para receber as últimas notícias sobre mercearia e alimentação todas as manhãs
Os anúncios de outono também incluirão murais detalhados fora de casa no centro da cidade, que reimaginam a herança da marca no Reino Unido, ao mesmo tempo que a exibem num formato moderno.
Mark Brown, diretor de marketing da Hovis Bakeries, disse: “Estamos muito satisfeitos que o anúncio ‘Strength Baked In’ esteja sendo amplamente divulgado em todo o país.

Esta campanha é um investimento na celebração da nossa herança, das nossas comunidades e da força duradoura que vem da bondade simples e saudável. ‘ “Os sinais fantasmas que inspiraram a campanha fazem parte da vida das pessoas há gerações. Mas esta é uma história contada através de lentes modernas.

Acreditamos que Hovis é mais do que apenas pão; é um símbolo de resiliência e um lembrete dos valores que nos unem hoje.” Isto marca um grande investimento na marca, reforçando a sua identidade como parte do grupo ABF mais amplo. Seu endereço de e-mail não será publicado.

title: Stay in the Game for You and Your Mob: New campaign puts First Nations voices at the heart of bowel cancer screening via 33 Creative
story: From performing at the Melbourne International Comedy Festival Galas to becoming a familiar face on Nine Network’s The Block, First Nations comedian and campaign spokesperson Andy Saunders brings his trademark humour and energy to the campaign, fronting a new television commercial encouraging mob to take action and do their bowel cancer screening test.
The Stay in the Game for You and Your Mob creative is a partnership between the Australian Government and Cancer Council, developed by 33 Creative for the National Bowel Cancer Screening Program.
It aims to make bowel cancer screening feel simple, normal and accessible, while encouraging mob to prioritise their health and take action early.

The new TVC features an all First Nations cast, reflecting the communities the campaign is speaking to and bringing authentic First Nations voices and experiences to the national conversation around bowel cancer screening.
Says Mayrah Sontor, Director of 33 Creative: “Having an all First Nations cast helps create a campaign that feels genuine, relatable and culturally relevant.

The collaboration between the Australian Government, Cancer Council Australia and 33 Creative demonstrates best practice in reaching First Nations audiences – ensuring culture, community and lived experience are reflected in the work.

This approach helps build trust and creates campaigns that genuinely connect with mob.” Says Saunders: “As a proud Biripi man and a dad, this campaign is personal to me. We look after our families, we look after our communities, but too often we put our own health last.
If taking a free bowel screening test could give you more time with your kids, your grandkids and your mob, then it’s worth doing.

I’m proud to stand alongside this campaign because it’s about breaking down shame, starting conversations, and reminding our people that looking after yourself is one of the strongest things you can do.”
Bowel cancer is Australia’s second biggest cancer killer, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people have higher rates of bowel cancer, making regular screening particularly important.
